patch_description: The current program fixes centers via a single hand-designed hex layout and solves radii exactly with LP, reaching sum=2.02. The new program keeps the exact LP radii solver (vectorized for speed) but makes it a subroutine inside a two-phase optimizer: (1) generate ~10 diverse base layouts (hex row patterns with several spacings/offsets plus jittered variants), score each cheaply via LP; (2) spend the remaining time budget (~2.0s deadline) doing adaptive-step random-restart hill climbing on the winning layout's centers — each move perturbs one circle center, and moves are accepted only if the LP sum increases; the step size anneals and resets on improvement plateaus. This exploits the fact that sum-of-radii is exactly the LP optimum given centers, so center moves directly optimize the objective. Time-based deadline avoids overrunning the eval budget.
